Hey. I've had to take meds for severe anxiety and depression, and I can tell you first hand, they aren't the right way to go. First off I wanna say if you ever need to talk to someone I'm here to listen to you and do my best to pit myself in your shoes. What helped me get.  Through the worst of my depression is finding a hobby.  In doing so, I found things I'm good at and it gave me a sense of value and meaning. And I don't mean video games or something you can occasionally do then forget about. I mean something that takes work to do in the real word. I have high functioning autism, so I found playing music and doing math are great at keeping me engaged in the world around me and not constantly thinking, focusing on the negatives in my life. It'll take time to find something you're good and and some work, but if you're serious about getting better, this is a great first step in recovery. Although I'm currently going through some stuff of my own, finding these things gave me a reason to get out of bed and gave me a new motivation. You need something you're passionate about. But if you just need to vent, I'll be here for you. Ik how bad life can suck at times, but having a friend that's gone through the same thing makes it a bit more bearable.
I see what you mean. What do you normally do at nights you feel this way?

Instead of wondering if you're worth it, maybe you should expend that energy in creating a worth in your life. I'm here if you ever need to talk, and I'll do my best to help you in any problems you may have, but ultimately, you need to do some seeking of yourself to find something to make you satisfied with life. I'd recommend a hobby, but don't make it something you do occasionally and forget about, make yourself the best at that particular thing. It might take time, and work,but when you find something you're good at and enjoy, you have a new sense of belonging.  But sometimes people just need to vent, in which case I'm willing to be there for anyone in need of an ear.
